title: Every process, natural or artificial, can be viewed as a computation

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Every process, natural or artificial, can be viewed as a computation

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Any process that follows definite rules, including processes in nature governed by physical law as well as processes constructed by humans, can be viewed as a computation, giving a uniform framework for comparing very different processes.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: all processes, whether they are produced by human effort or occur spontaneously in nature, can be viewed as computations.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 12, “The Principle of Computational Equivalence”; section “Basic Framework” (from p. 715), p. 715. Scope: all natural and artificial processes

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch12-01: not-empirically-resolvable, resolvability 0.08

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Examples can demonstrate that the framing is possible and useful, but cannot empirically establish a universal interpretive convention. The statement is not a distinct prediction about process behavior.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: One can map state transitions in any chosen rule-governed process to an input-output computation, but no observation distinguishes this optional representation from another exact description.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The claim proposes a conceptual framework.

The unrestricted quantifier and 'viewed as' provide no falsification criterion.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.1
analysis feasibility: 0.1
data existence: 0.1
discriminating power: 0.05
data adequacy: 0.05

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Calling a rule-following process a computation does not add a variable, a dataset, or a forbidden outcome. Whether nature in fact follows definite rules is a different and stronger statement than the one made here. As stated, the sentence is a framework for comparison, not a claim those comparisons can test.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: The claim says every rule-governed process may be regarded as a computation. Any process already given by definite rules satisfies that redescription, and no measurement distinguishes it from the same process described as law-governed evolution.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value: Can be viewed as introduces a uniform language rather than a distinct empirical commitment.
